advisories.title: Fall Armyworm Scouting Advisory — V3 to V6 Maize Stages
advisories.content: Sustained night temperatures above 18°C combined with humidity exceeding 70% for five consecutive days in Mukono District indicate elevated Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) risk. Maize fields currently at V3–V6 growth stages should be scouted within 48 hours. Recommended actions: deploy pheromone traps at field edges, handpick and crush egg masses and early instar larvae, apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or recommended neem-based biopesticides per MAAIF Crop Protection guidelines, and stagger replanting with NARO Longe 5 or Longe 10H in subsequent windows. Coordinate with sub-county extension officers for community-based scouting under the FAMEWS protocol.
advisories.farmer_segment: Smallholder maize farmers, Lake Victoria Crescent zone

advisories.title: Coffee Leaf Rust Prevention — Bushenyi Arabica Plantations
advisories.content: Recent weather observations across Bushenyi and surrounding districts show temperatures of 15–28°C and cumulative rainfall above 50 mm over the past month with relative humidity above 80%. These conditions are highly favorable for Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix) development on Arabica coffee. Farmers should apply preventive copper-based fungicides approved by UCDA, ensure proper canopy management to improve air circulation, plant or maintain shade trees (e.g., Albizia and Ficus species), and inspect lower leaf surfaces weekly for orange-yellow pustules. Coordinate with UCDA field teams for area-wide spray campaigns.
advisories.created_by: Dr. Peter Wasswa — UCDA Regional Coordinator

advisories.title: Bean Anthracnose Management — Flowering Stage Crops
advisories.content: Sustained rainfall above 20 mm with temperatures of 18–22°C across flowering bean fields in Mbale District indicates high anthracnose (Colletotrichum lindemuthianum) pressure. Farmers are advised to apply MAAIF-approved seed dressing at next planting, use certified disease-free seed of NARO short-season varieties (60–75 day maturity), practice crop rotation away from legume hosts for at least two seasons, and remove and destroy infected debris. Avoid overhead irrigation during flowering. Report severe outbreaks via the NAADS extension network.

advisories.title: Hass Avocado Phytophthora Root Rot — Drainage Advisory
advisories.content: Cumulative rainfall exceeding 150 mm over the past two weeks combined with soil temperatures above 25°C in Kabale orchards creates elevated Phytophthora cinnamomi risk. Hass avocado growers should improve drainage in low-lying blocks, avoid root disturbance and waterlogging, apply phosphonate-based trunk injections where permitted, mulch with well-decomposed organic matter (avoiding trunk contact), and source planting material from MAAIF-certified nurseries. Monitor for yellowing foliage and dieback as early indicators.

advisories.title: Robusta Coffee Twig Borer Response — Dry Season Stress
advisories.content: Prolonged dry conditions and rising daytime temperatures across Robusta coffee zones in the Lake Victoria Crescent are increasing Coffee Twig Borer (Xylosandrus compactus) pressure on drought-stressed trees. Recommended actions: maintain soil moisture through mulching, apply balanced NPK fertiliser to support tree vigour, prune and destroy infested twigs (showing characteristic dieback), avoid wounding during the dry season, and deploy ethanol-baited traps for monitoring. Coordinate with UCDA on community-level pruning campaigns.
advisories.farmer_segment: Robusta coffee smallholders, Lake Victoria Crescent

alerts.title: Coffee Berry Borer Emergence — Robusta Zones
alerts.description: Pheromone trap catches in Kibinge and surrounding parishes indicate Coffee Berry Borer (Hypothenemus hampei) emergence above the seasonal threshold. Robusta blocks with ripening cherries should initiate post-harvest sanitation and monitor for flight activity.

alerts.title: Fall Armyworm Population Spike — Central Region
alerts.description: FAMEWS community reports and pheromone trap data confirm a sharp Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) population spike across maize-growing sub-counties. Late-instar larvae reported in V6–V8 maize. Immediate scouting and Bt application advised.

alerts.title: Maize Lethal Necrosis Suspected — Eastern Highlands
alerts.description: Survey teams report mosaic and necrosis symptoms consistent with Maize Lethal Necrosis (MLN) on volunteer maize in Kapchorwa and Mbale. Confirmatory diagnostics at NARO Namulonge underway. Avoid moving green maize and control thrips vectors.

alerts.title: Heavy Rainfall Forecast — Lake Victoria Crescent
alerts.description: Seven-day forecast indicates cumulative rainfall exceeding 80 mm across Mukono, Luweero and Wakiso. Risk of waterlogging in low-lying maize and bean fields, and increased Phytophthora pressure in avocado orchards. Drainage advisories recommended.

alerts.title: Coffee Leaf Rust Pressure — Southwestern Highlands
alerts.description: Sustained temperatures of 15–28°C with relative humidity above 80% observed across Arabica coffee zones. Lower-leaf pustule counts are above the MAAIF action threshold. Preventive fungicide window open for the next 10 days.

pests.name: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda)
pests.climate_trigger: Night temperature >18°C, humidity >70% for 5+ consecutive days
pests.description: Migratory moth larvae that damage maize whorls. First detected in Uganda in 2016; present in all maize-growing districts. FAMEWS-monitored.
pests.recommended_actions: Whorl-stage scouting, Bt bio-pesticides, neem products, handpicking, staggered planting, pheromone traps

pests.name: Coffee Berry Borer (Hypothenemus hampei)
pests.climate_trigger: Temperature >20°C with high humidity; post-harvest period
pests.description: Small bark beetle that bores into coffee cherries causing yield and quality losses. Most damaging coffee pest globally.
pests.recommended_actions: Sanitation, Beauveria bassiana, pheromone traps, timely harvesting, full strip-picking

pests.name: Coffee Leaf Rust (Hemileia vastatrix)
pests.description: Fungal disease producing orange-yellow pustules on lower leaf surfaces. Major cause of Arabica yield losses.
pests.recommended_actions: Preventive copper-based fungicides, shade tree management, resistant varieties (e.g., NR 2017)

pests.name: Phytophthora Root Rot (Phytophthora cinnamomi)
pests.climate_trigger: Cumulative rainfall >150 mm in 2 weeks, soil temperature >25°C, waterlogged soils
pests.description: Soil-borne oomycete causing root rot and tree decline in Hass avocado. Spreads through water and infected planting material.
pests.recommended_actions: Improve drainage, phosphonate trunk injection, mulching, resistant rootstocks, certified nurseries

pests.name: Bean Anthracnose (Colletotrichum lindemuthianum)
pests.climate_trigger: Cool, wet conditions (18–22°C) with rainfall >20 mm during flowering
pests.description: Seed-borne fungal disease causing dark sunken lesions on stems, pods and leaves. Most common bean disease in Uganda.
pests.recommended_actions: Certified disease-free seed, crop rotation, seed dressing, removal of infected debris
